title: Checkpoint Climb
description: A rover records the elevation at each checkpoint. A checkpoint earns a signal when its elevation is strictly higher than every earlier checkpoint. The first checkpoint earns a signal when the list is nonempty. Return the number of signals.

examples.explanation: The elevations 3, 4, and 7 set new records.

title: Mirror Cargo
description: A cargo label contains lowercase English letters. A label is mirror-safe when reading it from either end gives the same sequence. Return 1 when the label is mirror-safe, otherwise return 0. The empty label is mirror-safe.
constraints: label contains only lowercase English letters

examples.explanation: The letters match from both ends.

title: Supply Pair
description: A station needs two distinct supply crates whose weights sum to target. Return their zero-based indices [i, j], where i < j. If several pairs work, choose the smallest j, then the smallest i. Return an empty array if no pair works.

examples.explanation: Indices 1 and 2 are the first pair completed while scanning left to right.

title: Quiet Windows
description: A sensor log contains 0 for a quiet minute and 1 for an active minute. Return the length of the longest uninterrupted quiet period.

examples.explanation: The two middle quiet minutes form the longest period.

title: Tile Rotation
description: A circular display shifts each tile one position to the right per tick. Return the tile order after ticks ticks. A tile leaving the last position reappears at the first position. An empty display stays empty.

examples.explanation: The last tile moves to the front.

title: Trail Compression
description: A trail recorder stores lowercase movement labels. Compress each maximal run by writing its letter followed by the run length, including runs of length one. Return the compressed string; an empty trail returns an empty string.
constraints: trail contains only lowercase English letters

examples.explanation: Three a labels, two b labels, and one c label form three runs.

title: Inventory Intersection
description: Two depots list item codes, possibly with duplicates. Return the distinct codes present in both depots, sorted in increasing order.

examples.explanation: The shared codes are 3 and 8.

title: Grid Fence
description: A map uses 1 for a garden cell and 0 for empty ground. Each cell is a unit square. Return the total length of fencing around all garden cells, counting boundaries with empty ground and the outside of the map. Separate patches and holes all contribute.
constraints: grid is rectangular and contains only 0 and 1

examples.explanation: Three connected squares have eight exposed unit edges.

title: Bracket Beacon
description: A beacon command contains only parentheses, square brackets, and curly braces. Return 1 if every opening bracket is closed by the same bracket type in proper nesting order, otherwise return 0. An empty command is valid.

examples.explanation: Every pair closes in the required nesting order.

title: Missing Marker
description: A trail should contain every marker from 0 through n exactly once, but one marker is missing. You receive the other n distinct markers in arbitrary order. Return the missing marker.
constraints: markers contains distinct integers from 0 through n

examples.explanation: Markers 0, 1, and 3 are present, so 2 is missing.

title: Relay Segments
description: A relay log records signed energy changes. Count the nonempty contiguous segments whose total energy change equals target. Segments are distinguished by their start and end indices.

examples.explanation: The segments [2,-1,2] and [2,1] each sum to 3.

title: Cooling Strip
description: A cooling strip is labelled with lowercase English letters. A usable section is a contiguous substring containing no repeated letter. Return the maximum usable section length.
constraints: strip contains only lowercase English letters

examples.explanation: The section bcaef has five different letters.

title: Beacon Coverage
description: Each beacon covers a closed interval [start, end] on a road. Combine overlapping or touching intervals into maximal covered intervals. Return the combined intervals sorted by start. Intervals that only meet at an endpoint are combined.
constraints: Each interval has two integers with -1000000 <= start <= end <= 1000000

examples.explanation: The first two intervals overlap and combine.

title: Gateway Distance
description: There are n gateways numbered 0 through n-1. Each pair in links is an undirected connection that costs one hop. Return the fewest hops from start to goal, or -1 when goal cannot be reached. A gateway is zero hops from itself.
constraints: Each link joins two distinct valid gateways; links are unique

examples.explanation: The route 0 → 1 → 2 uses two connections.

title: Battery Steps
description: A rover begins at index 0 of a row of pads. From pad i it may jump forward by any positive distance up to reach[i]. Return the minimum number of jumps needed to reach the last pad, or -1 if impossible. A row with one pad needs zero jumps.

examples.explanation: Jump from 0 to 1, then from 1 to 4.

title: Workshop Schedule
description: One workshop can host one booking at a time. Each booking is [start, end], occupying the half-open interval from start through just before end. Choose as many bookings as possible without overlap and return their count. A booking may begin exactly when another ends.
constraints: Each booking has two integers with -1000000 <= start < end <= 1000000

title: Reservoir Volume
description: A cross section of a reservoir consists of width-one columns with nonnegative heights. Water falls from above and escapes at either outer edge. Return the total units of water held between the columns after settling.

examples.explanation: The three interior columns hold 3, 1, and 3 units.

title: Repair Budget
description: A maintenance team has unlimited vouchers of each listed positive denomination. Return the fewest vouchers whose values total amount exactly, or -1 if that total is impossible. Zero amount requires zero vouchers.
constraints: Vouchers are distinct integers from 1 through 10000

examples.explanation: Two vouchers worth 4 each reach the total.

title: Ancestor Broadcast
description: A connected tree contains n relay towers numbered 0 through n-1. Each pair in links is a bidirectional connection. A message takes one second per connection. Return the greatest shortest travel time between any pair of towers.
constraints: links contains exactly n-1 distinct edges and forms a connected tree

examples.explanation: A farthest pair is towers 2 and 4, three links apart.

title: Parcel Multiplication
description: Each parcel has an integer factor. For every index, return the product of all factors except the factor at that index. Do not use division. The product of no factors is 1.

examples.explanation: For the first parcel, multiply 3 by 4.

title: Signal Reconstruction
description: A noisy transmission source contains lowercase letters. Delete any number of characters while preserving the order of those retained to reconstruct target. Count the distinct choices of retained source indices that produce target, modulo 1000000007. The empty target has exactly one reconstruction.
constraints: source and target contain only lowercase English letters

examples.explanation: Choose source indices [0,1,4], [0,3,4], or [2,3,4].

title: Turbo Relays
description: A directed relay network has n nodes and routes [from, to, cost]. Travel from start to goal at minimum total cost. You may use one turbo token on at most one route, replacing that route cost with floor(cost / 2). Return the minimum cost, or -1 when no route reaches goal.
constraints: Routes connect distinct valid nodes; directed pairs are unique

examples.explanation: Take the two-edge route and reduce one cost from 8 to 4.

title: Lane Capacity
description: A delivery network has n junctions and directed lanes [from, to, capacity]. Flow can split among lanes, but each lane carries at most its capacity and every intermediate junction must receive and send the same amount. Return the greatest total flow possible from source to sink.
constraints: 0 <= source, sink < n and source != sink
Directed lane pairs are unique and connect distinct junctions

examples.explanation: All five units leaving junction 0 can reach junction 3.

title: Partition Ledger
description: A ledger contains nonnegative workloads in fixed order. Split it into exactly groups nonempty contiguous batches. The processing time is the largest batch sum. Return the smallest possible processing time.

examples.explanation: Split after the third entry to obtain sums 14 and 18.

title: Rising Routes
description: A height map is a rectangular matrix. A route may start at any cell and move up, down, left, or right, but every next height must be strictly larger. Return the largest number of cells on one route.

examples.explanation: One route follows heights 1 → 2 → 6 → 9.

title: Wildcard Registry
description: A registry pattern contains lowercase letters, ? matching exactly one arbitrary letter, and * matching any sequence of letters including empty. Return 1 if the pattern matches the entire lowercase name, otherwise return 0.
constraints: name contains lowercase English letters; pattern additionally permits ? and *

examples.explanation: The star consumes e and the question mark consumes a.

title: Cut Network
description: A communication network has n nodes and undirected links. A critical link is one whose removal increases the total number of connected components. Return all critical links as [smallerNode, largerNode], sorted first by smallerNode and then by largerNode. The initial network may be disconnected.
constraints: Links are unique unordered pairs of distinct valid nodes

examples.explanation: Only the branch to node 3 disconnects additional nodes when removed.

title: Festival Packing
description: A festival receives an integer value for each time slot. Select exactly count nonoverlapping performances, each occupying exactly length consecutive slots. Unused gaps are allowed and adjacent performances are allowed. Return the largest total value of selected slots. If there is not enough room for all performances, return -1.

examples.explanation: Choose slots [0,1], [3,4], and [5,6], with sums 3, 8, and 12.

title: Detour Permits
description: A rectangular grid marks ordinary cells with 0 and restricted cells with 1. Travel from the top-left cell to the bottom-right cell, moving only one cell right or down at each step. Visiting each restricted cell consumes one permit, including the start and destination. Count routes using at most permits permits, modulo 1000000007.
constraints: grid is rectangular and contains only 0 and 1

examples.explanation: The paths right-right-down and down-right-right each use one permit.

title: Chain Bundles
description: A trader watches a sequence of daily unit prices. One transaction buys one unit on one day and sells it on a later day. Hold at most one unit at a time and complete at most limit transactions. Return the greatest total profit; skipping all trades is allowed.

examples.explanation: Buy at 2 and sell at 6, then buy at 0 and sell at 3.
